doc.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Featured on 'Conversations', Las Vegas show and tour with Eckstine
summary: Basie features Lewis's bass in the tune 'Conversations'; the band plays Las Vegas and the Million Dollar Theater, then tours with Billy Eckstine and George Shearing.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: band. Now all these guys, when they got together it sounded like they’d been playing for years together. So he said, “this is what I want, I can do something with this.” So we had a rehearsal. Let’s see, Nat Pierce brought some arrangements down, Nat Pierce from Boston. And Neal Hefti brought some, and somebody else brought some and put them down in front of him. Clark Terry and Wardell Grey used to pick up the music like this and never seen it before, and sing it, just like they were reading it with the horns, then put it down and play it. So I look at these guys, and I wondered if I could take this, you know it was difficult. And so he said, “No, don’t worry about it.” He said, “I’m going to feature you.” He said, “I never featured a bass before but I’m going to feature you.” I said, “when?” He said, “wait until we get this movie called ‘Conversations.’” I don’t know if you saw it or not. And through the whole movie, they couldn’t think of a tune, but he told me he said “What do you want to do? Do what you want to do and we’ll follow you.” So I said, “Well I’ve got a tune I’d like to do.” He said, “okay, we’ll call it ‘Conversations.’ So you play as if you’re asking a question, and then Clark Terry will come up and take a solo, and then you answer him with your bass, and then Wardell will come up and Buddy” and like that. And so they named the tune “Conversations.” And the thing went over well, man. And for a long time it played. And every once in a while now you see it on T.V. And he said, “It’s the first time I’ve ever featured a bass you know.” And then I got out and we went to the Million Dollar Theater. We played the Million Dollar Theater and they had an all-girl band there too came in once and we played, and as we left the theater, I think we went to Las Vegas. A club — a big club out there called the Trochedera or something like that at that time. I don’t know what it is now. But anyway, we walked in that club and we had the Norman Miller dancers, we had a girl singer, and I think we had Pearl Bailey’s brother, a dancer, and somebody else. But anyway we put on a show. That night we get on the big stage, they put those lights on, and everything looked different. I said, “this must be Hollywood.” So it was so beautiful when they put the lights on, and we played everything right down here until the show come on. People dancing all out there, and when it was time for the show to come on, Basie said, “all right that’s it, ‘One O’Clock Jump.’” We did “One O’Clock Jump,” man, everybody knew it, people would recognize it, they started applauding. We played that then the man announced the show and the show came on. We played that show, and when we got through, people just kept applauding. They wouldn’t stop. And so he had to play another tune you know. I think the tune — oh I can’t think of it now. But anyway we left there and we had to go back to California to the Oasis. And then we left and went on tour, with Billy Eckstine and let’s see some-body else. But anyway, Billy Eckstine was a big headline. And oh yeah, George Shearing, Billy Eckstine, and somebody else, there was three different, oh, the Nicholas Brothers.
